assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear, concrete discovery from nature: the first detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, which opened neutrino astronomy and later linked sources such as the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane to cosmic-ray origin. It fits my view that discoveries, not elegant ideas, come first.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit names only Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube. A prize for a discovery made by a large collaboration is awkward, and Halzen alone may be seen as under-crediting others such as instrument builders and analysts. I cannot verify from the supplied text who else would be named.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent lines of evidence (diffuse flux, point-source associations, Galactic plane) have accumulated over a decade, and the interpretation is stable. Timing looks ripe, though source identification is still partial.
uncertainties: Whether a single-person prize is fair for a collaboration-scale discovery.
The origin of most of the diffuse flux is still unresolved, so the full astrophysical story is not complete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the CMB into a precision laboratory and fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model (age, geometry, matter and dark-energy content). That is direct observational evidence on dark energy, close to my own field, and it has lasting impact on cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett as PI, Page as instrument and observational leader, and Spergel as principal theorist and analyst form a reasonable trio. Credit to the wider team and to predecessors such as COBE (already honoured) and Planck is a possible complication.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and refined by Planck and ground-based experiments; the results are very stable. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with COBE and Planck may make the Committee ask what is distinct about WMAP.
Persistent tensions (for example in the Hubble constant) do not undermine WMAP but affect how it is framed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation addresses the horizon and flatness problems and explains the origin of cosmic structure from quantum fluctuations, a question with existential weight. The nearly scale-invariant adiabatic spectrum seen in the CMB is a striking confirmation of the structure-formation part.
assessment.attribution: Credit is contested. Starobinsky, Sato and others made early contributions and Mukhanov with Chibisov is central to the fluctuation spectrum. The supplied names form a plausible but not uncontested trio, and I would want expert reports on priority.
assessment.maturity: Features of the CMB and large-scale structure support the framework, but the inflaton, the specific model and primordial gravitational waves are unconfirmed. As a theorist wary of unconfirmed ideas I regard this as an idea whose empirical core is strong but whose full content is not.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial B-modes; the specific inflationary mechanism remains undetermined.
Priority disputes (Starobinsky, Sato, Kazanas) and the supplied credit set may be incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a non-zero, relatively large theta-13 was decisive for the three-flavour neutrino picture and opened the way to searches for leptonic CP violation and the mass ordering. It is a clean, important measurement that complements the 2015 oscillation prize.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) announced in 2012; Double Chooz and T2K contributed too. The supplied trio is a reasonable but not unique configuration, and the fairness against Double Chooz and T2K would need examination.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several reactor and accelerator experiments with consistent precision, so the result is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K.
Whether committee views the result as incremental after the 2015 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler that ties the early-universe sound horizon to late-time dark-energy measurements. Its detection in galaxy clustering and its use in BAO surveys give strong, independent evidence about dark energy.
assessment.attribution: Sunyaev (with Zeldovich) is credited with the theoretical prediction, Eisenstein with the SDSS detection, and Cole with the 2dFGRS detection. Peebles and Yu, and Percival's later work, complicate this; the exact decisive contributions need expert advice.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across SDSS, 2dF, BOSS and DESI, so mature as a method, although the new dark-energy implications from DESI are still under discussion.
uncertainties: Complex credit among theory predictors and two simultaneous detections.
Evolving DESI results on dark energy might change the broader interpretation, though not the BAO detection itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kilonovae link neutron-star mergers to r-process nucleosynthesis, and the AT2017gfo event confirmed that gravitational-wave sources can be followed in light. It is an important multi-messenger and nuclear-astrophysics result.
assessment.attribution: The theory (Li and Paczynski, Metzger, Kasen), and the observation (Tanvir and others, with many teams) are spread across many people. The supplied trio is not obviously complete, and the 2017 discovery was a vast collaboration effort.
assessment.maturity: Based largely on one well-observed event plus a handful of candidates, so confirmation is less independent than I would like. It may be early.
uncertainties: Only one unambiguous kilonova with gravitational waves.
Broad authorship in the observation, and the relation to a possible gravitational-wave prize (2017) already given.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave band and may reveal supermassive black-hole binaries. This is a real clue from nature relevant to gravitation.
assessment.attribution: Several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA) reported similar evidence in 2023. The three supplied names represent leaders of different regional arrays, and the credit is hard to fit into three people.
assessment.maturity: Evidence is at about 3-4 sigma without a definitive Hellings-Downs detection and without a settled source; this seems premature.
uncertainties: Not yet a firm detection and the origin (binaries versus new physics) is open.
Large multi-collaboration credit that may not map to three persons.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gauge/gravity duality is the most influential idea in my own field, yielding tools for quantum gravity, black-hole information and strongly coupled matter. I recognise its importance, but I am sceptical about elevating it without a clue from nature.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 conjecture is the decisive step; Witten and Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov made the dictionary precise. Maldacena and Witten is a plausible pair but Polyakov and the GKP trio raise attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Mathematically tested in many ways, but it has no direct empirical confirmation in our universe; the Nobel tradition suggests waiting for experimental clues.
uncertainties: No direct experimental test for the physics it claims to describe.
Credit between Maldacena, Witten, Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov; only some are in the supplied list.
